names.note: The Greek form saint.gr prints in its own parenthesis: «Ο Όσιος Comgall (ή Comhghall) (Κομγάλλιος)». The day's line itself prints only «Άγιος Comgall», in Latin letters; the two Latin-letter forms Comgall and Comhghall are the page's own and are not recorded as a language form here, because the page gives no language for them.

birth.note: saint.gr: «καταγόταν από την Ιρλανδία και γεννήθηκε στην πόλη Ούλστερ το 517 μ.Χ.», and the head line of the same page gives «(517 - 602)». The page calls Ulster a city, which it is not, and that word is left as the page's.

death.note: saint.gr: «Ο Όσιος Comgall κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το 602 μ.Χ.», and the head line of the same page gives «(517 - 602)».

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Comgall»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **The day's line prints his name in Latin letters and nothing else**, which is why the stored form is the Greek one from the life page's parenthesis. **The corpus keeps no Comgall**, so this is a new folder and not an upgrade. **Two things on the page are hedged and are left hedged**: the three thousand monks are «Λέγεται ότι», it is said that; and Ulster is called a city, «στην πόλη Ούλστερ», which it is not, and the word is reported rather than corrected, on the rule that a reading which looks wrong is the source's. **His teacher Finnian has no folder** and is named in the life without a link. **`basil-the-great` is joined to him by the page's own sentence** — «Εφάρμοσε τους μοναχικούς κανόνες του Μεγάλου Βασιλείου» — which is a rule followed and not a dedication. **`locations` are left out**: Ireland, Ulster and Bangor are named and none is located further. No relics, no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
